originalTitle: Some US Fed officials considered rate hike on Iran war fallout, June meeting minutes reveal
simplifiedContent: Some leaders of the US central bank, also known as the Fed, recently met to discuss the state of the economy. They talked about inflation, which is when prices for things like food and housing go up, and some thought it was a good idea to raise interest rates right away to help control it. However, they ultimately decided not to raise rates for now. This is important because raising interest rates can affect how much it costs to borrow money, which can impact the overall economy. The leaders also thought that they might raise interest rates later this year, which could have a similar effect on borrowing and the economy.

originalTitle: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Thursday
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening in the stock market: Indian stocks had their biggest one-day drop since March due to higher oil prices, concerns about the Middle East, and negative trends in other global markets. This led to many investors selling their stocks, causing the decline. To know what will happen next, we need to watch for a few key things, including what's happening in the world politically, what companies say about their future earnings, and what central banks decide to do. These factors will help determine how the stock market moves in the near future. Analysts are paying close attention to these things to figure out what will happen next.

originalTitle: BofA cuts 2026 average gold forecast, sees long-term upside
simplifiedContent: Bank of America has lowered its prediction for the average price of gold in 2026 by 14%. This means they think gold will be worth less next year than they previously thought. Even though they still think gold will do well in the long run, other big banks like JPMorgan are also being cautious about their short-term predictions. Right now, gold is selling for around $4,060 per ounce, and different experts have different ideas about what will happen to the price. This change in prediction matters because it can help investors decide whether to buy, sell, or hold onto their gold investments.

originalTitle: Levi Strauss shares slip ahead of Q2 earnings report as investors await impact of FIFA World Cup campaign
simplifiedContent: Levi Strauss, a well-known clothing company, is about to release its quarterly earnings report, which is like a report card for the company's financial health. Before the report comes out, the company's stock price has gone down a bit. Investors are waiting to see how the company did financially, and they expect the company to say it made 24 cents per share in profit and had $1.52 billion in sales. This would mean the company's sales and profit grew compared to the same time last year, which is a good sign. The company's recent marketing campaign with the FIFA World Cup may have also had an impact on its finances, which investors are eager to learn more about.

originalTitle: Laser Power & Infra raises  ₹222 crore from anchor investors ahead of IPO
simplifiedContent: Laser Power & Infra Limited, a company that's about to go public, has already raised ₹222 crore from big investors who agree to hold the shares for a while. This was done at a price of ₹214 per share. The company is planning to raise a total of ₹742 crore through its initial public offering (IPO), which will start on July 9, 2026. The IPO will be open to different types of investors, including regular individuals, and the company's shares are expected to be listed on the major stock exchanges by July 16. This matters because it shows that big investors are interested in the company, which could affect how the IPO goes and the company's stock price.

originalTitle: SBI Funds Management files RHP for IPO; issue opens on July 14
simplifiedContent: SBI Funds Management, a company related to the State Bank of India, is planning to sell shares to the public for the first time through an Initial Public Offering (IPO). This means that people can buy shares of the company starting from July 14, 2026. The company is selling up to 203.71 million shares, with the State Bank of India itself selling 128.33 million of its own shares in the company. This is a significant event because it allows individual investors to own a part of SBI Funds Management. The IPO is an opportunity for investors to buy shares of the company, which can be a way to potentially earn money if the company does well.
